title: Discovery & The 4 Risks - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille
text: Discovery & The 4 Risks - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Our Courses Train Your Team Articles Just Now Possible Get in Touch Sign in Subscribe Discovery & The 4 Risks - All Things Product Podcast with Teresa Torres & Petra Wille Teresa Torres 10 Nov 2026 14 min Listen to this episode on: Spotify | Apple Podcasts In one of their most philosophical episodes yet, Petra Wille and Teresa Torres turn product thinking on the discovery practice itself. If you treat the continuous discovery habits as a product — and the organizations that buy training as the customer — do they actually have product-market fit? Teresa runs the idea through her own framework of the four big risks and lands somewhere uncomfortable: the habits work beautifully at the team level, but at the organizational level she’s increasingly unsure they can stick. Boards want predictable, up-and-to-the-right results; executives are rewarded for feeling certain and dictating solutions; and real adoption rarely survives a leadership change or a certain company size. The provocative question underneath it all — and it’s not a loss of faith in discovery: if organizations won’t change, maybe the solution has to. Key Takeaways Teresa turns the tables and treats the discovery habits as a product, with training-buying organizations as the customer — then checks it against the four big risks. This isn’t a loss of faith in discovery: at the individual and team level, the habits clearly work. The doubt is about the organizational level. Viability isn’t the problem — companies want better discovery and will pay for it. The risk shows up in willingness: reserving the time, pushing through busy weeks and blocked customer access. The deeper risk is organizational. For the habits to stick, the org has to change its structures — and that’s where it repeatedly breaks down. Boards reward predictable, up-and-to-the-right results; executives are incentivized to feel certain and dictate solutions — which breaks the trust discovery depends on. Lasting change seems to need a committed leader who stays a long time; it rarely survives a leadership change, and gets harder as a company grows past a small size. The reframe: maybe treat organizational constraints as fixed and evolve the solution to fit within quarterly results and existing incentives — rather than asking the whole org to change. Petra’s counter: even partial adoption is deeply valuable — once a team works this way, “what has been seen cannot be unseen.” Notable Moments “The blog post is titled, ‘Does Continuous Discovery Have Product-Market Fit?’” — Teresa “I wholeheartedly still believe in continuous discovery. That is not in question.” — Teresa “Once you work that way, what has been seen cannot be unseen.” — Petra “Maybe the problem is not the organization… maybe our solution is wrong.” — Teresa “If I was the only one facing this, I’d just conclude I’m not very good at this. But it’s not just me.” — Teresa Resources & Links: Follow Teresa Torres: https://ProductTalk.org Follow Petra Wille: https://Petra-Wille.com Mentioned in this episode: Teresa’s blog post, “Does Continuous Discovery Have Product-Market Fit?” — written but not yet published at recording and even now; this episode is a preview, and listeners are invited to write to Teresa with their take The four big product risks — desirability, usability, feasibility, viability (Teresa prefers “desirability” where Marty Cagan uses “value” in The Four Big Risks ) Petra’s experiments slide — her “tapestry” of experiments for de-risking the four risks Related episode: “Organizational Change Is Exhausting” HIPPO — the “highest paid person’s opinion” problem Dunbar’s number — referenced on the company-size threshold where adoption gets harder SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) — mentioned in Petra’s large-organization example Continuous Discovery Habits by Teresa Torres — the habits under discussion Join the Conversation: Have thoughts on this episode?
